target_customer: College students ordering snacks and convenience items, delivered by student riders
problem: Campus students wanted quick convenience delivery; large platforms took 30 minutes or more. Duffl promised 10 minute delivery from small campus storefronts.
business_model: Own-inventory convenience retail with student-run campus stores and delivery fees

founders.name: David Lin
founders.background_notes: YC page says he later founded Aligned.

founders.name: Brian Le
founders.background_notes: Self-taught software engineer per YC page.

founders.name: Rohun Vora
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder.

founders.name: Graham Farrell
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder, no bio.

technical_complexity.rationale: Ordering app plus scooter logistics; the difficulty was operations and unit economics rather than software.

defensibility.rationale: Campus density and the student-operator model were the only edges; incumbents with larger budgets could copy the service.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Sources name these as larger rivals but none is shown buying or copying Duffl; it was acquired in December 2025 by a smaller campus delivery operator.

market_need_then: Students wanted fast delivery; Duffl later reported four cash positive markets and 35,000 orders from 11,000 students in September 2022 (TechCrunch).

identity.voice_and_tone: Student-peer culture with named roles: riders are Racers, campus store heads are Admirals

branding.brand_signature: Racers and Admirals student roles with free merch and scooter perks
branding.community_and_virality: Campus newspapers (Daily Bruin, Daily Nexus, Wildcat, State Press) and a Berkeley business review wrote about it; student workers got free Duffl merch.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong campus word of mouth and distinctive role names, but the name is easy to confuse with duffel and no mascot was found.

outcome_analysis: Duffl grew from a UCLA 10 minute delivery service to several campuses and raised about 13 million dollars including a 12 million Series A in October 2021. Its UCLA headquarters closed abruptly in May 2024 amid worker complaints and restructuring, and Rev Delivery announced it acquired the company in December 2025. Terms and the specific cause of the decline are not public, so failure factors are left empty.
notes: Seed rests on one database (StartupIntros). Series A amount and date come from dot.LA (December 2021) and TechCrunch (December 2022, Volition lead, total over 13M); VCBacked lists Alumni Ventures, YC, 1984 Ventures, Volition and GoAhead (single aggregator, not recorded as investors beyond Volition).
